bifrost: springboard/src/shell/atspi/ (AT-SPI2 bridge), springboard/ui/src/ax.rs, springboard/sdk/src/lib.rs (controls_tree, ax_set), springboard/proto/src/lib.rs (Configure, reduce_motion, text_scale), springboard/src/shell/accessibility/mod.rs, springboard/src/shell/magnifier.rs, springboard/src/shell/assistive_touch.rs, springboard/src/shell/accessibility/spoken.rs, springboard/src/shell/accessibility/braille_out.rs, springboard/src/shell/audio_graph.rs, springboard/src/shell/earcon.rs (PopupCues), springboard/proto/src/axtext.rs (AxNotify), springboard/sdk/src/widgets.rs (toolbar and sheet groups), springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs (notification forwarding)
summary: BifrOSt covers a Linux AT-SPI2 screen-reader bridge (roles, states, text attributes, text events, announcements, element notifications as signals, secure fields) and system display settings (zoom, reduce motion, increase contrast, reduce transparency, larger and bold text) that apps can read. Screen reader earcons, Speak Selection and a Braille line are wired in the shell. The hierarchy API is used by the sidebar, toolbar and sheets only. No Accessibility Inspector, Switch Control or Voice Control is wired, and Braille output and audio graphs have no device or request path yet.

features.feature: System accessibility settings readable by apps

features.note: Apps receive reduce_motion and text_scale through Configure; contrast and transparency reach apps through the renderer (calendar-desktop follows them, see springboard/apps/calendar-desktop/CHANGELOG.md). No single SDK AccessibilitySettings struct. The accessibility_display service now returns increase contrast, reduce transparency, differentiate without colour, invert colours, reduce motion and dim flashing lights, and pushes options_changed on any change. Needs a Midget check. The shell itself honours Reduce Motion (desk.rs, mod.rs, switcher and jiggle through anim_ms), Reduce Transparency (vibrancy.rs, glass.rs, control_center.rs, desktop_bar.rs, quicksearch.rs) and Increase Contrast (ui.rs separators and material borders, appearance.rs colour contrast). Checked by reading the code, not on Midget.

features.note: Display Zoom sets a 1.0 or 1.15 geometry factor for apps. Screen zoom (Full Screen up to 8x, and a Picture in Picture lens that follows the pointer) is a presenter transform on the whole display. The magnifier app is a camera loupe with digital zoom and filters. Not verified on Midget. Checked 2026-10-17: no code change. The shell's own interface scale follows Display Zoom (shell/mod.rs sets ui.s from layout.s times the zoom) and apps receive the factor in Configure.zoom; the presets are Standard and Larger.
A floating Home button with six system shortcuts, plus hold-duration settings from 0.5 s to 2 s. No pointer-based keys or dwell control.

gaps: The sidebar, toolbar and sheet draw accessibility groups; the menu, the other immediate-mode kit helpers and non-view apps still publish flat lists.
Shell chrome is in the AT-SPI tree but read-only (press is not routed back) and Spotlight has no live text.
The AT-SPI bridge is untested on a live Orca; unit tests cover only wire round trips and mapping.
Spoken Content: Speak Items Under the Pointer is not built (the shell has no pointer-hover text source). Speak Selection (Option+Escape) is built.
Custom actions: an element's named custom actions are not exported on the AT-SPI Action interface ; they are listed and run through the shell's ax control command (src/shell/axmap.rs).
Braille: the reader's line is kept ready as cells, but no Braille display driver exists, so nothing reaches a device.
Audio graphs: a graph can be rendered and played, but no SDK call or shell path requests one.
